beur-hagra/1:א: (א) On parchment or etc. like Torah scroll. There on the book; gemara derives writing from writing etc.; follows his view in ch. 1 Laws of Tefillin that Torah scroll is not invalidated by being tied with straps — see there.
beur-hagra/1:ב: (ב) And if he wrote it [with other materials]. And likewise in a Torah scroll — one should not infer that each alone invalidates; kankantom in the Mishnah implies it is not [valid] ink, and the same for a Torah scroll as in Shabbat 103b: if he wrote not with ink, etc. And in Yerushalmi Megillah ch. 1 halacha 11 they must write with ink; and afatzim water implies in Gittin 19a it is not ink except when both are together — then it is ink — and it teaches us that even if it is not erased as in Eruvin 13a, nevertheless it is permitted; and he ruled like R' Yehudah from R' Meir who said to each one throw in, etc., as in Laws of Tefillin ch. 1 — and this is their language: how is ink made? They gather smoke of oils, etc., soak it in afatzim water and the like and write with it that if erased it would erase — and that is the ink of optimal mitzvah to write a Torah scroll with. And if he wrote all three in afatzim water and kankantom that stands and is not erased — they are valid. If so, what did the halacha transmitted to Moshe at Sinai exclude — that they be written in ink — to exclude other dye types such as red and green and the like; that if he wrote in a Torah scroll even one letter in other dye types or in gold — these are invalid. And so wrote the Rosh in small halakhot. And this is what he says here: he wrote in other [materials], etc. And this is his language in his commentary on Sotah ch. 2: I saw in Eretz Yisrael they distance Torah scroll writing with one ink type called in Arabic chibur — only real ink; and here he erred in pesak halacha from the gemara, for the last thing said in the gemara on this matter: each throws in kankantom except the sota parsha in the Temple; and the copyist there said: as copyist I saw to explain what is chibur — as the Geonim explained: chibur is afatzim ink and they throw kankantom into it, a type of blackening earth that is not erased; and so wrote R' Chananel, etc. — see there.
beur-hagra/1:ג: (ג) And it requires ruled lines. On every line — unlike Levush and Magen Avraham; they erred, for regarding tefillin that do not require ruled lines we say thus as in Tosafot Gittin 6b on the matter beginning R' Yitzchak said etc.; and if you say etc.; and Rabbenu Tam says etc.; and likewise in Agudah; but mezuzah and anything that requires ruled lines perforce we require on every line; and see there and in Rosh.
beur-hagra/1:ד: (ד) And there is no hide, etc. This follows his view that he ruled even a mezuzah does not require processing lishmah; and although regarding a Torah scroll we hold it requires processing lishmah as they said in Gittin 54b, and so he ruled in chapter 10 of laws of Torah scroll and chapter 1 of laws of tefillin — they hold thus.
beur-hagra/1:ה: (ה) And some say it requires [processing lishmah]. This is Rabbenu Tam's view as he wrote in Menachot there, in the passage beginning "until," etc. Rabbenu Tam says halacha is Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel as the sugya of damages follows him; and that in the chapter "the judgment was finished" where Abbaye and Rava disagree, etc. — Rabbenu Tam and R' Chananel explained Rava like Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel who requires processing lishmah; and perforce invitation is not a thing — for if not, it would be possible with skin cutting and small repairs, etc.; and so he wrote in Sanhedrin there — see there; and so he ruled regarding mezuzah; and see siman 32 and Yoreh Deah siman 288.
beur-hagra/2:א: (א) B or on. It’s a call in the final name:
beur-hagra/2:ג: (ג) As a book of Torah. Mordechai and the Magistrate are taught in the name of his sons, and as the Ramban said, “We are taught, in particular, the scriptures.” She is like a book of Torah and written and true to teach none of her writing as a book of Torah and written a book to teach anything that is not a body such as the dissolution of Dina As a book of Torah and assimilate it, per the fact that it is not a mere body in the cow’s womb, and therefore it is said that the reader is embodied as a box that is outside your body The reader of the scroll is what is not in the Torah, and in the chapter of Kama, there is nothing between books and the age of Esther that the books are written in every tongue It means Heaven for all this and it is lawful. And there is a second chapter in one verse that says one book and one verse says: How easy it is in its scope “It means that it is rejected in its wake and not in the rest of it:

beur-hagra/2:ט: (ט) And regarding missing and extra [letters]. Menachot there; and see Tosafot there, passage beginning "but extra," etc.; and as written 29a, 34a — even a tip of yud; and Ran Megillah ch. 2.
beur-hagra/2:י: (י) Also required [to utter orally]. Megillah 18b: let us find support for him, etc.; baraita: R' Shimon ben Elazar said, etc. And in Yerushalmi Megillah ch. 4 halacha 1 — R' Zeira in name of Rav Chananel: even one expert in Torah like Ezra should not review from his mouth and read, as in Bereishit, etc.; and it was taught: incident of R' Meir who was in Asia and there was no megillah written in Hebrew and he reviewed from his mouth and read — we do not learn from a time of duress. And some say two writings: he wrote the first from his mouth and wrote the second from the first and hid the first and read from the second.
beur-hagra/2:כ: (כ) And to utter every word, etc. Menachot 30a; and see there Tosafot s.v. and Moshe, etc.; and so Mordekhai Laws of Megillah siman 457 — from here one can prove a Torah scroll scribe must utter with his mouth, etc.; and so all poskim; and likewise in Shulchan Aruch Yoreh Deah siman 274 seif 2 — and it implies that even if he writes from a written copy — for 98 cannot write it not from a written copy; and what is written siman 32 seif 31: if he is not, etc. — tefillin is different; and Magen Avraham there; and this is R' Yeshaya's view who inferred from Semag's language: it is forbidden for another person to prompt the scribe unless he returns, etc.; and one could say for emphasis he cited it even though when another prompts him he need not err as in blessing of kohanim — nevertheless it is required as we find with Moshe: even though the Holy One blessed be He speaks, nevertheless Moshe returns and speaks; and so all poskim who did not divide; and a Torah scroll requires from a written copy even though a Torah scroll requires from a written copy.
beur-hagra/2:מ: (מ) And it requires [a pole and blank], etc. Bava Batra 13b; and see there Tosafot s.v. and makes. It appears to R' Yitzchak we read: and makes at its head for surrounding and at its end to roll a pole; and so emended the Geonim there 14a: all books roll to their beginning; and there 14b: Ezra's book rolls to its beginning; and Yerushalmi Megillah ch. 1 halacha 11: they make a pole for a book at its end — for Torah from here and from here; therefore the book rolls to its beginning and Torah to its middle; and so in Mishneh Torah ch. 2 and Yadim ch. 3: R' Yishmael — at the end it is not tamei until a pole is made; and see R' Shimon there and the Rosh; and even to Rashba who upholds the reading "books" and distinguishes between glued, etc. — he admits regarding books alone one makes a pole at its end, etc.
beur-hagra/2:נ: (נ) And some say it needs tagin and some say not, etc. Ran ch. 2; and the first reasoning holds it is a matter of the body and its law is like a Torah scroll as above; and the last reasoning holds tagin are not from the body of writing as in Menachot they found for the Holy One blessed be He tied crowns, etc. — see there; and anything not of the body does not impede; and we do not say it is called a book since one must learn from writing in a scroll, etc. — from gezeirah shavah of ketivah ketivah and not learn from sefer; and see Ran and Rashba; but in Shabbat 104 that without adornments it is not letters at all; and Ran; and Mordekhai Padua; and see what is written siman 35 seif 3.
beur-hagra/2:ס: (ס) They also used. And he is a great sign and a great sign:
beur-hagra/3:א: (א) Seif 3 — if he divided above the writing, etc. Tur's language and per Rashi there and Ran and Mordekhai there.
beur-hagra/3:ב: (ב) And if not. Yerushalmi ch. 3 halacha 8: ten sons of Haman and kings of Canaan, etc. — for a mitzvah or to impede, etc. R' Ba bar Zavda passed and they asked him and he said in name of Rav: to impede.
beur-hagra/4:א: (א) Seif 4 — must extend. Tur's language; and it implies from their words like the first language in its writing since it is written in this siman in laws of writing.
beur-hagra/4:ב: (ב) In writing and writing. Rashi and Rashi:
beur-hagra/4:ג: (ג) And requires, etc. Yerushalmi there: R' Yirmiyah bar Bun — must be ish at the head of the page and et at its end — swayed and descended like this beam — meaning like two beams of a pocket equal on both sides like builders' balance; and see in Mishneh Torah there. And what is written at the head of the page means at the head of the line and at the end of the line — not as some explain at the head of the column, for otherwise why would R' Yirmiyah add after R' Yirmiyah in name of Rav who said there ten sons of Haman, etc., and song of 48, etc., one column above, etc. From this is drawn what they write ten sons of Haman in a column by itself in large letters. And the confusion is that we were not given to write ten sons of Haman in large script letters; rather the main point of what is written at the head of the page is at the head of the line as above. And R' Yirmiyah himself teaches: if from R' Yirmiyah in name of Rav one would say since ten sons of Haman were separated from all songs and equated to the song of 48 — for the matter that both are written alone one column above, etc. as above and as in the gemara — if so we would equate them entirely not to write within ten sons of Haman the word before it as in the song of kings of Canaan that begins "king," etc.; and this is what R' Yirmiyah said: must, etc., ish at the head, etc., and as above at head of line and end of line like pocket eye and two beams as above and like other megillah letters.
beur-hagra/6:א: (א) Seif 6 — and because it has various explanations. Rashi and Tosafot explained one [stitch] in its middle and two in its fourth parts; proof from what is written in Makkot 9 that three must be plaited etc.; and Rif explained two at the corners, proof from what is written in Eruvin 57 three villages that are triangular etc.; and likewise in Bechorot 38 regarding blemishes; and see chapter HaAreil, chapter there; and likewise Rambam explained, except he explained three threads in every stitch like a triangular heifer and triangular goat etc.; and see there in Targum; and see in Rosh there and in Tosafot and in Tosafot Bechorot 39a s.v. sheyehu etc.
beur-hagra/6:ב: (ב) And if there are none [sinews], etc. As in Bava Batra 162b: supports, etc.; do not wonder, etc. Mordekhai and Hagahot Maimoniot ch. 2 s.k. 60 — reason: it must be entirely hollowed from head to end that it be one book alone except the sewing margin as in Shulchan Aruch Yoreh Deah siman 275 seif 1; and as in Gittin 60a: a book lacking even, etc.; and Rosh explained no sewing with it; and as written there seif 4; and Yerushalmi Megillah ch. 3: sewing halacha 11; and so Rambam Megillah ch. 2: the megillah must be sewn entirely until all its hides are one megillah.

peri-megadim/1:_: In afatzim water, etc. — his intent from Gittin 12a: they wrote a get in mei milin and afatz — valid; and Tosafot there and Hagahot Ashiri: at first glance afatz is not Mishnah ink; they answered when mixed, etc.; and Taz wrote on what Rama said: one can say afatz is chibur — ground gallnuts kneaded in water writing with it — not included in ink; but mei sheriyat afatzin or kneaded is ink; and the word with beit seems should be without — Magen Avraham did not bring Kol Mefareish. And know Shulchan Aruch brought Rambam ch. 2 Megillah halacha 9 specifically on gvil and klaf — not on duchsustos; and in Laws of Torah scroll Rambam invalidates Torah scroll on duchsustos; and Yoreh Deah siman 271 seif 3 wrote on gvil and klaf and did not finish if duchsustos invalidates Torah scroll; and in Mishnah it says on paper and hide invalid — implies duchsustos since paper is not valid; nevertheless ch. 2 Megillah see our master no processing lishmah required; and what not mentioned equal lines for megillah — from where; and per this on klaf and gvil not duchsustos; and from that it should be written on the scroll — specifically gvil and klaf — from where implied; and in Hagahot letter 30 in name of Semag proof megillah written among Writings individual fulfills — see there implies written with them one processing; and so Bach in name of Semag; Bach wrote see Tur; and Rabbenu Tam wrote R' Hai does not disagree what preceded; and one can say from Mishnah stam on paper invalid implies duchsustos valid; and Rabbenu Tam wrote to say it has all Torah scroll law — if so per those who invalidate duchsustos in Torah scroll — same megillah; see Tur. Rosh validates all in Torah scroll; and it appears l'chatchila not to write megillah on duchsustos and same Torah scroll per Rambam; and so Magen Avraham will explain further.
peri-megadim/2:א: (א) Also afatz, etc. and I did not understand — behold they leave section for its circumference at head; and as there is dispute on pole (wood they attach at head or end) or head or end — so dispute on section; since so — should leave section at head and end; and further they act and roll from end to head; also possible to satisfy both views — pole at head and end; and what he wrote in name of Rashba explained siman 690 Magen Avraham letter 15: listener must hear every word — only listener need not intend each word — see there; and there I wondered on responsum language — here cannot extend.
peri-megadim/2:ב: (ב) Behold Mechaber wrote requires surrounding hide each letter surrounded and tagin on chet two zayins, etc., and hanging of hei and kuf — all like Torah scroll per Rabbenu Tam alone except what is noted in commentary not equal to Torah scroll; and if to tag — also gimel tzadi hei brought two views; and from processing no difficulty — proof from megillah among Writings as said; and in Bach see Tur and Hagahot Maimoniot wrote need not tag it — meaning unlike Rabbenu Tam; perhaps his intent tagin too are Torah scroll laws — only what noted in commentary equal to Torah scroll; difficult here; and as I wrote; also tagin on chet — in Torah scroll scribes are not accustomed to tagin; all the more megillah; and siman 32 that scribes were exact wrote tagin — not other scribes (and there is somewhat proof from what is written not to make hei like chet); and Yoreh Deah 274 used tagin in Tur and Shulchan Aruch tagin; Magen Avraham siman 36 letter 3.
